validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — the wiki page's sole cited source is 'Annual Statistics Bulletin, OPEC, 2012, p.75'. The literal live URL (opec.org/.../ASB2012.pdf) returns HTTP 200 but the bytes are actually the OPEC homepage HTML (soft-404/redirect target served with a 200 status) -- confirmed via `curl` + `file`: the downloaded 'PDF' is 'HTML document text'. This is a materially dead link, and would be a strong existence-flag on its own if that were the end of the trail. However the same file is preserved on the Wayback Machine (archived 2025-01-10) as a genuine 7.8MB PDF (confirmed via `file`), and pdftotext extraction of pages 70-80 (Table 4.10, 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', Libya section) contains a discrete, exact-match row: 'Intesar/Sahel | Sirte Oil | 80 [mi] | 30 [in] | 19,824,412 [1,000 scm/yr]'. This is NOT a generic/aggregate mention -- it specifically names this segment by both endpoints. Unit conversion: 80 mi x 1.609344 = 128.75 km, rounding to GEM's LengthKnown=129.00 km; diameter 30 in is an exact match to GEM's Diameter=30.00 in; capacity 19,824,412 thousand scm/yr = 19.824412 bcm/yr, matching GEM's Capacity=19.82 bcm/y to two decimal places. All three quantitative fields match precisely -- this is very likely GEM's own original source for this row, so it resolves existence/provenance (the entity is not a GEM-only hallucination -- the sheet's own citation, once actually retrieved, does name it) but is not an independently-corroborating second source for the spec values themselves. General plausibility is reinforced by the wider Sirte Basin gas-gathering context: the Intisar field (var. Intisar/Intesar, discovered 1967, Sirte Basin) is a well-known major Libyan oil/associated-gas field, and this exact same OPEC table lists an unbroken, internally-consistent chain of adjacent Sirte-Oil-operated segments through the same numbered junctions -- Intesar/Sahel (this row) -> Sahel/km-81.5 (roster P1871, 49mi/30in/19,541,206 -- matches P1871's 79km/30in/19.54bcm) -> km-81.5/Brega (roster P1868, 82mi/30in/8,496,177 -- matches P1868's 132km/30in/8.5bcm) -- a coherent, internally-consistent multi-segment corridor rather than an isolated/implausible entry. CLASSIFICATION -- correct. This is OPEC's own 'Gas pipelines' table (not the oil-pipelines table earlier in the same document), and Intesar/Sahel sits among Libya's other named Sirte-Basin gas trunk lines at transmission scale (19.8 bcm/y), not a small gathering/process line -- no reclassification needed. DUPLICATE -- checked against all 30 roster rows, in particular P1856 'Intesar-Brega Gas Pipeline' (Intesar Oil field->Al Wahat, 333km/42in/42.48bcm), which shares the 'Intesar' endpoint and looked like a candidate duplicate/relabel at first glance. The SAME OPEC table resolves this: it separately lists 'Intesar/Brega | Zueitina | 207 [mi] | 42 [in] | 42,480,884' as its own distinct line item -- 207mi=333.1km (matches P1856's 333km exactly), 42in (matches P1856's 42in exactly), 42.480884 bcm/y (matches P1856's 42.48 exactly) -- a DIFFERENT owner (Zueitina, not Sirte Oil) and different route/spec from the Intesar/Sahel/km-81.5/Brega chain. So P1856 is a separate, independently-operated direct Intesar-to-Brega line, not a duplicate or aggregate of the Sirte-Oil segmented chain that P1870 belongs to -- both are real, distinct, and correctly split. No other roster row references 'Sahel' as origin or shares this route/spec combination. ATTRIBUTION -- minor caveat, not scored as an error: GEM records Owner1='Libyan National Oil Corp' (100%); OPEC's table attributes the line to operator 'Sirte Oil' (Sirte Oil and Gas Manufacturing Company), a wholly NOC-owned subsidiary independently confirmed as state-owned/NOC subsidiary by a 2013 Canadian IRB research response (ecoi.net) -- consistent with how sibling rows in the same OPEC table (P1868, P1869, P1871, P1872, P1867, etc.) were already assessed in this sweep. NOC-as-ultimate-owner is defensible; Sirte Oil Company would be the more precise operator entry. SPEC -- confirmed, no material disagreement (see existence section: all three fields match within rounding). LOCATION -- only StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea=Libya can be supported; neither the gem.wiki page's own Location section, nor OPEC's table, nor general search names a city/province for the 'Intesar' or 'Sahel' waypoints (Sahel appears to be an internal Sirte Oil network junction name, not a settlement), so I left city/province unresolved rather than guessing. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION -- could not find a second, fully independent source naming this exact 'Intesar/Sahel' segment (general Sirte Basin infrastructure writeups, USGS Minerals Yearbook Libya, and 2026 Libyan NOC/PGJ/Libya Observer network-upgrade news all discuss the broader Intisar/Sirte Oil gas-gathering system but none names this specific 80mi/30in segment) -- so tier=medium rather than high, matching the pattern already established for the sibling km-marker-chain rows (P1868, P1869, P1871) in this same sweep.
